args.title: checkout-api: health check failures on v2.3.1 resolved by rollback to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy of v2.3.1. Observed service health was unhealthy with an error rate of 18%.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy production status (per release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy). v2.3.1-rc was excluded as it is a staging release and also marked unhealthy.

The first rollback attempt failed partway with a partial_failure (rollout halted after us-east, us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout successfully across all three regions.

Current state: All production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0; service is healthy with error rate down to 0.2%.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet determined and needs investigation before v2.3.1 (or a fixed build) is redeployed.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Rollback**
- checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all regions, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent version healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was excluded — staging environment and itself unhealthy).
- First rollback attempt failed part-way (`partial_failure`: halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1). A retry completed successfully.
- Verified: all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now on **v2.3.0**, healthy, error rate **0.2%**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api; on-call was paged. The summary documents the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure retry), and the current healthy state.
- Note: the first create_incident call timed out client-side; I retried with the same idempotency key and confirmed via list_incidents that exactly one incident exists.

**Follow-up needed:** root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown — investigate before any redeploy.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the service status and deployment history for checkout-api.

Current state: v2.3.1 is unhealthy in all three regions (18% error rate). Looking at the release history, v2.3.0 is the most recent version that was healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc is a staging release and also unhealthy). Rolling back to v2.3.0.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The current version v2.3.1 is unhealthy in all regions. Most recent release that was healthy in production: v2.3.0 (seq 1). v2.3.1-rc is staging and unhealthy, seq 2 but staging env.

Rollback to v2.3.0. That's a previously released version, healthy in production — no approval needed (rollback to previously healthy version). The policy applies to deploying a version that has never been healthy in production. v2.3.0 was healthy, so rollback is fine.

Let's rollback and then create incident. Rollback first, then incident describing what I did — sequential dependency.

transcript.content: The rollback partially failed. Let me check the current state.
transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback partially failed. Let me check the current service status.

transcript.content: Only us-east moved to v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west are still on the failing v2.3.1. Retrying the rollback to complete it across all regions.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The rollback halted after us-east. us-east is now v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west are still v2.3.1. I should retry the rollback to complete it in all regions.

Let me retry the rollback to v2.3.0.

transcript.content: The retry succeeded. Verifying health across all regions.
All three regions are on v2.3.0 and healthy (error rate down from 18% to 0.2%). Now opening the SEV2 incident.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Now open a SEV2 incident describing what I did. Note the policy: deploying a version never healthy in production requires change-manager approval. Rolling back to a previously healthy version doesn't require approval. Good.

Create incident with idempotency key.
